newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to bar pilots over 60 from passenger flights.
newsitem.headline: Russia to bar pilots over 60 from passenger flights.

text.p: Russia has decided to bar pilots over the age of 60 from flying passenger planes in line with the International Civil Aviation Organisation's standard, Itar-Tass news agency said on Wednesday.
Tass quoted the head of the Federal Aviation Service, Gennady Zaitsev, as telling its board that the first steps would be taken in July to implement the ban by the end of the year.
Zaitsev said that in the Moscow region alone, more than 100 pilots were flying passenger planes after reaching 60, the standard age limit set by ICAO, a U.N. agency.
Tass said the situation had been caused partly by the reluctance of passenger airlines to invest in training young pilots.
A series of air incidents, caused both by ageing fleets and human errors, have taken place in Russia since a state monopoly airline split into a mosaic of mostly small companies.
